title: Strong Electronics Growth 2026
gist: Electronics production growth accelerated through 2026 worldwide, with Taiwan more than doubling on Nvidia AI module demand and the U.S. at 8.1%, Japan 17.6% and the EU 16.9%. Meanwhile IDC reports Q3 2026 PC and smartphone shipments fell 20% and 22% as AI-driven memory demand pushed memory costs up 350% year over year.

insights.claim: U.S. electronics production grew 8.1% (three-month average versus a year ago) in August 2026, continuing an accelerating trend since October 2025.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Broad industrial demand for electronics is strengthening, not peaking.

insights.claim: Japan's electronics production growth swung from a 1.5% decline in January 2026 to a 17.6% increase in August 2026, and the EU 27 went from a 10.5% decline in January to 16.9% growth in July 2026.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Sharp reacceleration outside Asia suggests the AI hardware cycle is lifting regional supply chains.

themes.theme: Taiwan doubling on Nvidia AI modules

insights.claim: Taiwan's electronics production more than doubled in 2026, with three-month-average growth over 100% for most months, driven largely by demand for Nvidia AI modules whose ICs TSMC makes and which other Taiwanese firms assemble.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Taiwan's electronics output is a direct proxy for Nvidia AI server demand.

themes.theme: AI memory squeeze hits PCs and phones

insights.claim: According to IDC, PC shipments in Q3 2026 fell 20% year over year and smartphone shipments fell 22%, and IDC projects full-year 2026 declines of 11.3% for PCs and 13.9% for smartphones.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Consumer device OEMs face a sharp volume downturn in 2026.

insights.claim: AI applications are driving huge demand for DRAM and flash memory, pushing memory costs up 350% year over year in Q3 2026 per IDC, and those shortages and prices are the main cause of falling PC and smartphone shipments.

insights.so_what: Memory makers win pricing power while PC and phone OEMs lose volume and margin.
